title: Cyril Hilsum invented the flat-screen displays that hold us in thrall
summary: This Economist obituary honors Cyril Hilsum, a British physicist who invented the active matrix LCD technology that powers virtually all modern flat-screen displays, from smartphones to laptops. His breakthrough work at Royal Signals and Radar Establishment in the 1970s replaced bulky cathode-ray tubes with thin, lightweight screens, enabling the mobile computing revolution.
problem_solved: Enabled flat, lightweight screens to replace bulky CRT monitors, making portable devices like smartphones and laptops possible
why_valuable: His invention laid the technological foundation for the entire mobile computing era and the $100+ billion display industry
